tagline.text: A 19th-century neoclassical church of St. James the Greater at the heart of Ibaan town

children.text: Ibaan Church is the church of St. James the Greater (Santiago Apostol) in the center of Ibaan, an inland Batangas town. Its cornerstone was laid in 1853 and the main building was completed in 1869 in a neoclassical style. It became an archdiocesan shrine of the Archdiocese of Lipa in June 2022 and is also known for its Easter dawn traditions of Bati and Dagit.
Ibaan is an inland town of Batangas, about
13km
from Batangas City and about

from Manila. The church stands in the Poblacion (town center) and its official name is the Archdiocesan Shrine and Parish of Saint James the Greater. Locals simply call it Ibaan Church, and it is also known by its Spanish name, Santiago Apostol. Wikipedia and the parish listing on ParishPH both name St. James as the patron saint, so it is correct to call it the church of St. James, not St. Jerome. Per Wikipedia, the coordinates are about 13.82 degrees north and 121.13 degrees east.

The church's history goes back to the Spanish colonial era. According to Wikipedia and local Batangas history sources, a small chapel was built in 1784 in what is now Barangay Matala, and the first church and convent were built in the town proper in 1817. Ibaan separated from Batangas in 1832, and the parish listing also gives 1832 as the founding year of the parish. Because sources disagree between 1817 and 1832, it is safe to read 1817 as the start of the first church construction and 1832 as the town's independence and the parish's founding.

The present building took shape in 1853, when the Augustinian priest Manuel Diez Gonzales laid the foundation stones. The first plans are said to have been drawn by the architect Luciano Oliver. Fr. Bruno Laredo began the twin towers in 1865, and the facade and roof were completed in 1869. Fr. Vicente Maril then finished the towers in 1876 and reworked the facade. In all, construction work of one kind or another continued for nearly 50 years.

The architectural style is a simple neoclassical. The building has a cruciform plan, and its facade has a triangular pediment with a rose window above and square belfries on both sides. The front has round Ionic columns and wooden doors carved with geometric patterns, and the choir loft area has arched openings. The main materials are said to be adobe stone and cement. Wikipedia points out that cement was later applied to the facade and regards it as an unfortunate restoration, since lime mortar is the traditional method. It is not a large building, but like many small-town churches it sits right next to the town plaza, the market and the main road, so it is easy to explore on foot. Over the years the church has also been through many disasters. An earthquake in 1880 damaged the building, and Fr. Francisco Alvarez repaired it from 1891 to 1896. A May 1942 earthquake brought down the towers, and the rebuilt towers were rededicated on January 31, 1947. During World War II the convent served as a temporary hospital for sick soldiers released from the Capas camp. One account says a provincial Eucharistic Congress was held at this parish around 1935, but other sources date it to 1937, so the exact year could not be confirmed. Stories like these make the church more than a place of worship; it is regarded as a building that holds the memory of the people of Ibaan.

blocks.title: St. James the Greater as patron saint and shrine status since 2022

children.text: The church was declared an archdiocesan shrine of the Archdiocese of Lipa on June 16, 2022. The parish is now run by priests of the Oblates of St. Joseph (OSJ) and belongs to the Saint Joseph the Patriarch vicariate of the Archdiocese of Lipa.

blocks.title: Twin towers and a neoclassical facade

children.text: With its triangular pediment, rose window and Ionic columns, the facade is typical of an inland Batangas town church. The towers were completed in 1876 and restored in 1947 after the 1942 earthquake.

Inside, the cruciform plan has a reredos behind the altar, and there are various decorations along the choir loft and side walls. Photos on Wikipedia also show a Lumen Christi Chapel, so it is best to ask the parish whether it is open. Some accounts mention an altar and ceiling restoration around the 2017 bicentennial, but this is poorly sourced. It is best to look around quietly during the day when no Mass is being held, and because the altar area is where worshippers pray, please observe good manners when approaching it.

Wikipedia states that a Philippine historical marker was installed in 1941. However, local Batangas history sources do not mention a marker, so we recommend looking for it on site and confirming for yourself.

Ibaan is known for its Easter dawn traditions of Bati (a greeting dance) and Dagit. In the Bati, a Kapitana in a white costume and straw hat dances with a white flag, and the Dagit is described as a variant of the Salubong (the Easter meeting). One blog reports that the church is too small, so the events are held outside.

blocks.title: Parish feast on July 25 and the dawn procession on the 25th of every month

children.text: The parish feast is on July 25 in honor of St. James. According to the parish listing, a 5:00 AM dawn procession of St. James is held on the 25th of every month, and a 5:00 AM Rosary procession on the first Saturday of each month.

blocks.title: A walk around town and Ibaan food

children.text: Many accounts introduce Ibaan's specialties of tamales and kulambo (handmade mosquito nets) at the plaza and market around the church. They are easy to see together with the church on a short visit. The whole town is small enough to walk, so you can link the church, market and plaza into a stroll of about an hour.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: A church visit that fits into a Batangas itinerary

children.text: Set out for Ibaan from Batangas City or Lipa. By taxi it is described as about
30 minutes
from Batangas City.
Walk once around the front of the church first, taking note of the towers, the pediment and the Ionic columns.
If no service is on, go inside and quietly look at the altar, the choir loft and the side walls. Please refrain from taking photos during Mass.
Stroll the town around the church and try tamales and local snacks.
Move on to Taal Heritage Town or Batangas City.
Mass times need to be confirmed locally, as noted below. Visiting just after the 6:00 AM weekday Mass or around midday will be much quieter.

items.title: Easter dawn route
items.subtitle: A day to see the Bati and Dagit

children.text: The timing of the Easter dawn events changes every year, so confirm it in advance through the parish contacts and arrive early.
Follow the procession along the town streets and watch the Bati and Dagit in sequence.
After the morning Mass, have a meal at a restaurant in town and head back.
The parish decides the venue and order of the events, so check the latest announcements.
Ibaan is about
from Manila, and booking sites estimate a trip of about
3~4 hours
. Alps The Bus from the Buendia terminal and Jam Liner from Cubao are listed as serving the Ibaan direction.
Bus schedules and fares change often, so check with the company before you leave.
From Batangas City to Ibaan is about
13km
, roughly
30 minutes
by taxi. Taking a bus from the Batangas Grand Terminal toward Lipa and transferring to a vehicle for Ibaan is also described, but it takes much longer.
Jeepneys or vans from Lipa toward Ibaan are said to run, so ask locally for the vehicle going to the Ibaan Poblacion.
The church is on the main road of the Poblacion, so you can walk to it once you get off in town.
Many people take a tricycle for short rides in town; confirm the fare locally.

From the Manila side, the usual route is through the SLEX and STAR Tollway toward Lipa and Batangas. The road in front of the church is narrow, so check for parking on nearby streets or on open ground near the town market.
The church is open year-round, and it is better to time your visit to event dates than to the weather. From November to May there is less rain, so walking around town is comfortable.
To see the Easter dawn Bati and Dagit, check the Holy Week schedule and the parish announcements. The July 25 parish feast and the December 30 Thanksgiving Day can be crowded with events.
Town-level events include the Les KuhLiemBo Festival on
February 11
and the flower festivals in
May
. If a church visit is your goal, allow plenty of time, because the whole town gets crowded on such days.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
Ibaan is a small town with few places to stay. Most visitors stay in Batangas City or Lipa and make a day trip. Hotels and restaurants are far more varied in Batangas City.
Ibaan tamales are well known, and you can try local snacks around the town market and plaza. Opening hours and prices differ by shop, so check on the spot.

If you have time left after seeing the church, walk around Bro. Medrano Plaza and the Recto Gymnasium in Ibaan town. Timing your visit with the town's official events, the Les KuhLiemBo Festival every
February 11
, the barangay flower festivals every
May
and Thanksgiving Day on
December 30

, makes the church visit much richer. Dates can change from year to year, so check the municipal announcements. Kulambo, a mosquito-net handicraft industry, is presented as Ibaan's signature craft and, together with tamales, is considered a symbol of the town.
Visits and photography may be difficult during Mass, so avoid those times.
According to the parish listing, weekday Mass is at 6:00 AM, and on Sundays there are Masses at 5:00 AM, 6:30 AM, 8:00 AM, 9:30 AM and 5:00 PM. These may change, so check the latest announcements.
Avoid shorts and sleeveless tops, and dress modestly with your shoulders and knees covered.
You can confirm event dates and times through the parish contacts (0915-5476282, 0922-2826559) or the Facebook page ASPSJG.
Combining Batangas City and Taal Heritage Town makes for an efficient one-day plan.
When the heat is intense during the day, take a rest in the shade inside the church.
When searching for the church, use Ibaan Church or St. James the Greater Parish to get the exact location in a map app.
This is still an active parish church, so respect Mass and prayer times and keep quiet.
Opening hours and the Mass schedule can change, so confirm with the parish before you visit.
Roads in town can be congested and crowded during Easter and the parish feast.
Follow the on-site guidance on whether photography is allowed inside.
Travel information sites disagree on founding years and earthquake years, so treat the years in this article as approximate.
If you drive, watch the parking and traffic on the narrow town roads.
Batangas's best-known Spanish colonial heritage town, a good addition to a church-visiting itinerary together with Ibaan.

from Ibaan, with a terminal and hotels.
